big_idea: Concurrent code uses parallel lanes. Two actions in the same time-step run together.
learning_intention: We are learning to write code with concurrent events.
student_learning_goal: I can write code with concurrent events.
success_criteria: I can write 2-lane code with at least 4 time-steps.
I can include a loop in my code.
I can predict where both robots end.
lesson_specific_materials: OPTIONAL: Buzz and Patch — if available; otherwise teacher voices both characters in two distinct voices, or substitutes two stuffed animals / paper-bag puppets / pictures on the anchor poster. Activity is unaffected.
Code Step Cards (30) and Loop Cards (8)
Lesson 2 writing tracker — provided in assessment_suite stage

minds_on.hook: Buzz writes code: Robot 1 forward + Robot 2 forward at the SAME time. Buzz adds a loop. Buzz opens: 'every LANE, every STEP, gets an ACTION!'
minds_on.teacher_script:
Bring children to the carpet. Buzz + Patch puppets. 'Yesterday we IDENTIFIED concurrent. Today we WRITE 2-lane code with a loop.'

Introduce vocabulary. Write REPEATING on chart. 'Repeating means doing the same action many times — a LOOP. Loops can be in concurrent code too.'

Demonstrate. Write on chart:
Step | Robot 1     | Robot 2
  1  | fwd         | fwd
  2  | turn right  | fwd
  3  | Repeat 3: fwd | fwd

'Step 3: Robot 1 has Repeat 3: forward — that means R1 forwards 3 times. While that happens, R2 forwards ONCE (or 3 times if synchronised).'

Discuss synchronisation. 'When R1 has a loop and R2 has a single step, they may finish at different times. That's OK. Code says what each robot does.'

More examples:
- R1: Repeat 4: fwd. R2: Repeat 4: fwd. Both forward 4 — synchronised.
- R1: Repeat 5: fwd. R2: turn turn turn. R1 finishes 5 steps; R2 turns 3 times.

'Buzz says — concurrent code can have loops in either lane. Each lane's code runs simultaneously with the other.'

'Today you WRITE 2-lane code with at least 4 time-steps and 1 loop.'
student_actions: Watch Buzz write 2-lane code with a loop.

steps.instruction: Whole group: write 2 codes together. (a) Both robots forward 5. (b) R1 forward 3, R2 turn turn turn fwd.

Three stations. Station A: Synchronised — pair writes 3 codes where both robots do the same. Station B: Different — pair writes 3 codes where R1 and R2 do different actions. Station C: With Loops — pair writes 2 codes with at least 1 loop in each.
Stretch challenge at Station C: write code where R1 has 6 steps and R2 has 3 steps. Predict ending positions.
Discuss the time-step model. 'Each row is one moment. Both lanes' actions happen in that moment.'
steps.teacher_prompt: Demonstrate on the grid mat with both robots.

steps.instruction: Circulate to record formative evidence on the writing tracker.
steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Ask 'Show me where both robots end.' Mark the tracker.

steps.instruction: STRATEGY COMPARE: Two pairs share their concurrent code that produces the same outcome. Class compares: same time-steps? Same length? Cite Grover & Pea (2013) on CT abstraction — many concurrent solutions can produce the same outcome.
steps.teacher_prompt: Buzz: 'Different code, same outcome — concurrency lets you choose the path.'

differentiation.for_emerging: Stay at Station A. Synchronised actions only.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Act out as 2 robots. NO-MATERIALS PATH: use floor tape or two parallel rows of desks as the 2-lane mat; children walk the lanes.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Three signals: writes 2-lane code; includes loop; predicts ending positions.

discussion_prompts: What does CONCURRENT mean in code?
How does a loop work in concurrent code?
What if R1 and R2 finish at different times?
Show me your code's ending positions.
consolidation.exit_routine: Buzz's writing refrain — 'every LANE, every STEP, gets an ACTION!' (3x). Each child writes one complete 2-lane code with no empty cells.

assessment_in_this_lesson.rationale: Lesson 2 captures C3.1 mastery for concurrent writing.

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child writes 2-lane code where R2's lane is empty for some steps — repairing the empty-lane confusion at Grade 3
expanded_walkthrough.rationale:
On writing concurrent code, the trap is the empty-lane error: child fills lane 1 with all moves and leaves lane 2 empty for some rows (Bers 2019; Grover & Pea 2013). Without per-row, per-lane completion, debugging downstream cannot ground.

Yesterday Buzz read concurrent code; today we WRITE it. Lesson 3 finds bugs; Lesson 4 fixes; Lesson 5 capstones.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Pair is at Station B. R1: fwd, fwd, turn, fwd. R2: fwd, [blank], turn, [blank]. Child says 'done'.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'You filled R1 but R2 has empty rows. What does R2 do in step 2 and step 4?'

The child looks. 'I forgot.' 'OK. Each robot needs an action every step. Either an action OR write WAIT to mean stay still.'

Walk through. 'Row 2: R2 ___. Maybe wait. Or fwd. Pick.' Child writes 'wait'. 'Row 4: ___. Pick.' Child writes 'wait'.

Generalise. 'Buzz says — every lane, every step, has an action. WAIT is a valid action for staying still. No empty cells.'

If still leaves empty: provide a 'wait' card. 'When R2 has nothing to do, write WAIT.' Force the no-empty rule.

Long-term recovery: every 2-lane code has an action in every cell.
expected_student_responses: (Mid) Fills cells with WAIT when prompted.
(Stretched) Uses WAIT strategically (e.g., R2 waits for R1 to catch up).
common_misconceptions: Empty cell means nothing. (Repair: every cell needs an action, even WAIT.)
WAIT is not a real action. (Repair: WAIT is intentional staying still.)
I can leave R2 blank. (Repair: each robot has a column; every row has an action.)
recovery_moves: DIAGNOSTIC A — child writes lane 1 only: drill 'every LANE, every STEP, gets an ACTION (or WAIT)'; child fills empty cells with WAIT.
DIAGNOSTIC B — child uses different actions per lane but skips rows: row-by-row checklist; child checks each row before advancing.
DIAGNOSTIC C — child writes correct concurrent but doesn't match outcome: trace the code on the lane mat; child physically walks the result.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Independent practice of C3.1 (write concurrent code).

parts_outline.task: Write a 2-lane code with 4 time-steps where both robots are synchronised.
Write a 2-lane code with a loop in one lane.
Write your own 2-lane code (4-6 time-steps) and predict the ending positions.

expected_image_assets: 2-lane template with loop slot for Part 2
